Honey, 5'4 and 109 pounds is NOT fat. It's a perfectly healthy BMI, maybe even a touch underweight (going by the "100 lbs. at 5 feet tall, 5 pounds for every inch thereafter" rule, which is generally how I gauge my own weight).

I know we focus on being slim here, and that can make it seem like anything more than bones is fat...but that is NOT the case. You are not fat. You do not need to lose weight right now, and you certainly shouldn't be embarrassed to be a perfectly lovely weight.

I'm sure that intellectually you know this, and I know it's not as simple as, "Just accept that you're not fat and quit worrying about it," at all...but I thought perhaps hearing it from someone else might help. (And I've actually meant to say something along these lines to you for a while now.)

I am so glad it helped you. IMO part of being a healthy thin person is accepting that even those of us who eat carefully and watch our weight can occasionally gain a pound or two. Like right now it's so hot that I haven't been walking the dog for our usual 4-5 miles a day every day; we've hit that number some days, but not every day like we did before the weather really heated up. So I've gained a pound in the past couple of weeks. No big deal. I am still thin, my clothes still fit just fine, and because I am thin it will be easy to lose that pound; I've already eliminated half of my evening snack (and am working on getting into a walking routine that avoids the heat better), and I know that by this time next week that pound will be gone. I'm not panicking and I'm not deciding that since I'm a pig I might as well be a pig and I'm not frantically cutting back all of my food. (I'm also a little period-bloaty at the moment, too, sigh.)

In other words, when we're thin we have a little leeway; it's one of the perks of being thin. A pound is not the end of the world. 98 lbs. is still a perfectly healthy and attractive weight for someone your height.

Same height here, I'm what you could call fully (weight) recovered at 118lb. Over the span of a year, I went from 94lb to this, where I'm fluctuating +/- 3 lb. Never really took pictures while anorexic, because I didn't care and was in a bad mental state, waiting to die eventually. I can tell that I am bigger now, and while it's not true, I feel so much bigger. I see myself much bigger. Although sometimes, I see myself alright I guess (not fat). Apart for a desire in me to still be underweight every now and then, I don't want to die anymore, don't fear many foods anymore (still liquid calories are a big eh to me), don't have breakdowns daily, don't restrict (not even count anymore). I work out but not as a punishment. Not being unnecessarily cold anymore all the time, no pain in my knees and ass when I lay down and sleep, no muscle spasms, my period is back. The eating guilt is mostly gone. It can get better. I got help. I recovered for the wrong reasons, but I am here to stay in this shape. My strongest addiction ever has for most part, faded. It takes a lot of work and mental strength to do this, maybe even a lot of time - take as much as you need, but what awaits on the other side is a happy resolution usually (at least in my case).

I still don’t drink liquid calories, they freak me out. The only good thing is that liquor has been cut out of the diet. Still have to plan all my food and I can’t eat spontaneously. You sound like you’re doing much better. I know it’s a struggle to keep the weight on and keep the bad thoughts out.

I am. I am amazed at the mental progress too. For anyone suffering of this fucked up retarded shit, trust me - once you start getting nutrients and feeding the brain more, things will change. The biggest change YOU need to do mentally, is attempt to diminish the triggers that make you restrict, or binge, or whichever your addiction is. For me it was extremely high levels of stress, loneliness, too high expectations and too little control over some things. I worked on those. It's not over yet and it will never be, maybe. I realize some other people will have it much harder, but at that point, anything is worth more than becoming numb and waiting to die. And finding hobbies and enjoying things (genuinely enjoying) for the first time in so long...it's worth the mental discomfort of food, feeling full, even gaining weight.
SO glad you're better, and btw, you have probably the best username here.
